physical_harm: The deceased suffered injuries leading to his death, but the court found no evidence that the appellants caused any injury to the deceased.
number_of_offences: 70 accused were charged; 13 were convicted, including the appellants.
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the deposition of the eye witnesses PW3, PW4, and PW6 but found that there was no concrete evidence that the appellants caused any injury to the deceased or participated in the commission of the offence.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses (PW3, PW4, and PW6) as providing deposition, but found that their accounts did not establish the appellants' involvement in the offence, and there was no concrete evidence of what was uttered by the accused.

legal_representation.state: Ms. Diksha Rai, Ms. Ragini Pandey, Debojit Borkakati

prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the appellants, as office bearers of the labour union, spoke something in their own language to the labourers, which led to their agitation and the subsequent attack on the deceased, thereby justifying the conviction under Section 302 IPC with the aid of Section 149 IPC.
defence_argument: The defence argued that there is no concrete evidence that the appellants caused any injury to the deceased or participated in the commission of the offence. They were present as office bearers trying to control the situation, and there is no evidence they instigated the mob.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that for a conviction under Section 302 IPC with the aid of Section 149 IPC, there must be concrete evidence that the accused participated in the commission of the offence or instigated others to do so.
